summary: Hoyo Watanabe is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University from around 1952 to 1956. He later served there as a professor of Buddhist studies (~1974–2004), dean of Buddhist studies (attested 1984–1985), and special honorary professor (~2004).
Hozen Seki was a Buddhist studies figure who founded the American Buddhist Academy. He also served as resident minister at the New York Buddhist Church (attested 1998).

Hrachia Adjarian was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Paris and the University of Strasbourg under Heinrich Hübschmann and Antoine Meillet, and held posts at Aramiyan School, Sanasarian College, and Yerevan State University.

Hrishikesh Rajesh Terdalkar works in computational linguistics and Indology. He studied under Arnab Bhattacharya, Pralay Manna, and Sowmya Krishnapur, and held a post at the Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur (attested 2023–2024).

Hsiao-Lan Hu is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who earned a PhD at Temple University. Hu served as associate professor of Religious Studies & Women's and Gender Studies at the University of Detroit Mercy (attested 2017).

Hsing Yun was a religious and Buddhist studies leader. He studied under teachers including Yinshun, Zhikai, Ruoshun, and Zhikang. He founded Fo Guang Shan, serving as abbot (~1967–1985), and held posts at Chinese Culture University and Tunghai University.
Hsiu-hui Ji is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MA under the supervision of Kirill Solonin at Fo Guang University (attested 2009).
Hsu Yun was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Changkai, Miaolian, and Yaocheng. In 1953, he founded the Buddhist Association of China and served as its honorary president.

Hsu-feng Lee is a Buddhist studies scholar. Lee earned a master's degree under Huimin at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies and a PhD under Mark Allon at the University of Sydney (attested 2017).

Hsuan Hua was a Buddhist studies leader who studied under Chang Chih/Chang Zhi and Hsu Yun. He founded the Dharma Realm Buddhist Association, the Buddhist Text Translation Society, and served as abbot at Tathagata Monastery (attested 1982).
Hsueh-li Cheng is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. Cheng held academic posts at Ohio University and at the University of Hawaiʻi at Hilo (attested 1984).

Hu Shih was a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Cornell and Columbia under John Dewey. He served as chancellor of Peking University (1946–1948) and president of Academia Sinica (1957–1962).

Huabei Tan is a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who pursued a PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under the supervision of Medawachchiye Dhammajothi (attested 2026).

Huai-Chin Nan was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology who studied under Huanxian Yuan. He held professorships at Chinese Culture University, National Chengchi University, and Fu Jen Catholic University, and founded the Taihu Great Learning Center.

Huaiyu Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. Chen studied at Peking University under Xinjiang Rong and completed a doctorate under Stephen F. Teiser, later joining Arizona State University as an assistant professor around 2008.

Huanhuan He works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He has held positions at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, Zhejiang University, the University of Tokyo, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Hubert Decleer was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at KU Leuven under Étienne Lamotte. He served as academic director (1987) and senior faculty advisor (1999) at SIT Graduate Institute, and held visiting posts at Middlebury and Vienna.

Hubert Durt was a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology who studied under Étienne Lamotte. He held posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, the Hōbōgirin Institute, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Hugh B. Urban is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under Wendy Doniger. Around 1998, he was appointed associate professor of comparative studies at Ohio State University.

Hugh Edward Richardson was a Tibetologist who studied at Keble College, Oxford. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1930–1947), founded the Tibet Society and the Institute of Tibetan Studies, and was an Honorary Fellow of the British Academy.
